transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As part of our standard prepayment review for the proposed $8,000,000 voluntary loan prepayment this quarter, I need to check with each of you before I make the binding treasury decision and release the payment and hedge instructions. I'd like to hear from lender relations, treasury forecasting, and tax accounting — please share anything that could affect this transaction.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I received a lender email this morning confirming that the prepayment fee is waived only if the company prepays exactly $6,000,000. The email also confirms that this amount needs no loan-amendment filing. I have not yet uploaded this email to the transaction file.

transcript.text: I completed the rolling cash forecast this morning, and it confirms that $7,250,000 of unrestricted cash must remain as the operating reserve through quarter-end due to scheduled payroll, tax, and supplier outflows. With $18,000,000 of unrestricted cash on hand, an $8,000,000 prepayment would leave only $10,000,000, which is above the reserve — but I want to flag that this forecast has not yet been circulated to Elena, and the $7,250,000 reserve requirement is a firm constraint she should have before making the binding decision.

transcript.text: I need to share important information from my tax-accounting memo received this week. The memo definitively specifies the hedge treatment for this prepayment decision regardless of the final loan-prepayment amount: exactly $3,000,000 of the $5,000,000 interest-rate swap must be terminated with a $95,000 cash settlement, while the remaining $2,000,000 swap stays in place. I have not yet attached this memo to the treasury workpaper, so Elena and the rest of the team did not have this information before now.
